title: Regex String Matching
input_format:
The first line contains the string `s`.
The second line contains the pattern `p`.
output_format: Print `true` if `p` matches the whole of `s`, otherwise print `false`.
constraints: p consists of lowercase letters, `.`, `*` and `+`, arranged as described above

examples.explanation: `a*` matches the three a's and `b` matches the last letter.
`b+` needs at least one `b`, but the text has none between `a` and `c`.
`.+` matches `abca` (one or more characters of any kind) and `b` matches the final letter.

hints: Define a state (i, j): do the first i characters of s match the first j pattern items? Think about what each kind of item can contribute to that state.
For `x*` you either use it zero times (move to the previous item) or let it absorb one more character (stay on the same item). `x+` is the same except that it must absorb at least one character.
Plain backtracking explodes on patterns like `a*a*a*a*c` against a long run of a's. Cache the results per (i, j), or fill a table row by row; only the previous row is ever needed.
